This revision incorporates the answers to the seven open questions raised in
v001. The decisions, in brief:

1. **Cards represent both tabs and windows** — a user-selectable grouping
   toggle (v001 assumed per-tab only).
2. **Thumbnails are scaled HTML captures** (as proposed), lazy-loaded with a
   capture queue and cache.
3. **Rename is triggered by right-click** on a window name (the existing
   double-click / pencil paths remain unchanged).
4. **Card sizing hotkeys are `[` (shrink) and `]` (grow)** — not
   `Ctrl` `+`/`-`, avoiding any conflict with browser zoom.
5. **The new spec filename format is adopted**
   (`SPEC-<version>-v<NNN>-<Name>.qmd`); the three 4.0.2 spec files were
   renamed to match and `spec-conventions.qmd` updated (done alongside this
   revision).
6. **Card view gets full 2-D arrow-key navigation**; sidebar↔tabs area
   switching moves to `Ctrl` `←`/`→`.
7. **Natural sort confirmed** for window names.

Sections unchanged from v001 are restated here in full so this document
stands alone.

> **Extended in place (2026-07-31, second Q&A round):** after approval of
> the above, a review of the whole interface for right-click opportunities
> was run item-by-item. Its outcomes are Requirements 5 (context menus) and
> 6 (sleeping-tab auto-wake), plus amendments to Requirement 3 (rename now
> lives inside the window context menu, with batch numbering) and to the
> thumbnail fallback notes.

## Requirement 1 — Numeric sorting of window names

### Current behavior and root cause

Window names are compared as plain lowercase strings in three independent
sort sites, so `window10` sorts between `window1` and `window2`:

- `components/Sidebar.tsx` — `sortedWindows` (the sidebar window list;
  default sort is by name ascending, so this is where the misordering is
  most visible).
- `App.tsx` — `getSortedTabs`, `case 'window'` (the "Window" column sort in
  the All Tabs table).
- `components/TabListView.tsx` — `displayedTabs`, `case 'window'` (the same
  sort duplicated for uncontrolled/AI-group tables).

The name *generator* (`services/nameGenerator.ts`) already produces
un-padded `window1`, `window2`, … — no change there, and **no zero-padding
will be introduced**.

### Design (decided: natural sort)

Add a single shared comparator in a small new module
(`services/sortUtils.ts`) and use it at all three sites:

```ts
export const compareWindowNames = (a: string, b: string) =>
  a.localeCompare(b, undefined, { numeric: true, sensitivity: 'base' });
```

`localeCompare` with `numeric: true` is a *natural sort*: any run of digits
inside a name is compared by numeric value, so
`window1 < window2 < … < window10 < window11`. Custom/AI names without
digits sort alphabetically among themselves, and mixed sets interleave
(`Project 2 < Project 10`; `Research` sorts by its first character against
`window…`). Confirmed as the desired rule in Q7.

Only the comparator is shared; the three duplicated sort implementations
stay where they are.

## Requirement 2 — Card view for tabs and windows

### View toggle and grouping (decided: both, user-selectable)

- A **Detail / Card** toggle (list icon / grid icon segmented control) is
  added to the header toolbar next to the existing preview toggle.
- When card view is active, a second small control appears beside it:
  **"Cards: Tabs | Windows"** — the user-selectable grouping from Q1.
- Both choices persist across sessions (`chrome.storage`, see
  [Persistence](#persistence-settings-schema)).
- The toggle applies everywhere the tab list renders: All Tabs, By Window,
  sidebar-checkbox filtering, and each AI group (each group renders its own
  grid under its heading; the *Windows* grouping applies only to the
  All-Tabs-style views, since AI groups and By Window mode are not
  window-shaped collections — there the control is disabled with a
  tooltip).
- Search, sorting, checkbox multi-select, selection/preview, keyboard
  navigation, and the close action all keep working in card view; sorting
  controls move into a small sort dropdown in the toolbar when card view is
  active (there are no column headers to click).

### Grid layout

Cards are laid out with CSS grid:
`grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(var(--card-width), 1fr))`
— they wrap automatically and are responsive to window and pane width.

### Tab cards

Each tab card shows:

- a **thumbnail** of the tab's page content filling the card (see
  [Thumbnails](#thumbnails)), and
- a **metadata overlay** hovering above the thumbnail (semi-transparent
  scrim anchored to the bottom of the card) so the user sees both the page
  and the data. Default field order matches the requested priority:
  **icon → last accessed → tab name → domain → window name**.

If the visible metadata does not fit, the overlay itself is scrollable
(`overflow-y: auto` with a max height). The browser natively scrolls the
innermost scrollable element under the pointer, so the hover-governed
behavior falls out for free: wheel over a card's overlay scrolls that
overlay; wheel anywhere else scrolls the main grid.

The selected card gets the same indigo ring treatment as a selected row;
checkbox and close (×) sit in the card's top corners (visible on
hover/selection, like today's row actions).

### Window cards

In the *Windows* grouping, each card represents one browser window:

- **Thumbnail:** the window's active tab's page capture (cheapest honest
  "view of the window's contents"; a 2×2 mosaic of the first four tabs is a
  possible later upgrade).
- **Overlay:** window name, tab count badge, and most-recent
  `lastAccessed` across the window's tabs.
- **Interactions:** single-click selects the card; **double-click drills
  into that window** (switches the dashboard to By Window view for it); a
  hover **↗** button focuses the actual Chrome window; **right-click opens
  the window context menu** (see Requirements 3 and 5). Window checkboxes
  mirror the sidebar's merge-selection checkboxes.

### Card sizing (decided: `[` / `]` hotkeys)

- **GUI control:** a compact slider in the toolbar (visible only in card
  view) plus `−` / `+` stepper buttons, adjusting card width between
  ~160 px and ~480 px in steps, with a reset affordance (double-click the
  slider handle) returning to the default (~240 px).
- **Hotkeys:** **`[` shrinks, `]` grows** (chosen in Q4 over
  `Ctrl` `+`/`-` to leave browser page-zoom untouched). Active only while
  card view is shown and no input field has focus (the existing keydown
  handler already ignores `INPUT` targets). No modifier needed; no browser
  shortcut conflicts.
- The chosen size persists across sessions.

### Thumbnails (decided: scaled HTML captures)

Chrome gives extensions **no way to screenshot a background tab**
(`chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab` only captures the active tab of a
window). Confirmed approach (Q2): reuse the mechanism the Preview Panel
already uses — `getTabContent` in `services/tabService.ts` captures the
page's HTML via `chrome.scripting.executeScript` — rendered small:

- Each card renders the captured HTML in a sandboxed `<iframe srcDoc …>`
  scaled down with `transform: scale(…)` (`pointer-events: none`, same
  `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` and injected `<base>` tag as the Preview
  Panel), so the thumbnail is a genuine miniature of the page.
- **Lazy + bounded:** thumbnails are captured only for cards visible in the
  viewport (IntersectionObserver), fetched through a small concurrency
  queue (e.g. 4 at a time), and cached per tab id + URL so re-scrolling and
  re-renders don't re-inject scripts. Off-screen cards drop back to the
  cheap placeholder to bound memory.
- **Fallbacks:** sleeping (discarded) tabs, restricted pages
  (`chrome://`, Web Store), and capture failures show a placeholder —
  large favicon + domain on a neutral background, with a moon badge for
  sleeping tabs. Card view never **mass**-wakes sleeping tabs just to
  thumbnail them; only the *selected* tab auto-wakes via the settled-
  selection rule (Requirement 6), and the Preview Panel's "Wake up &
  preview" button remains as a manual fallback/retry.
- **Known risk (accepted in Q2):** JS-heavy pages may look imperfect in
  miniature, and ~170 tabs make performance the riskiest part of this
  feature. If the lazy/bounded design still proves too heavy in practice,
  the fallback (a future revision) is placeholder cards with live
  thumbnails only for the hovered/selected card.

### Metadata configuration (Settings)

- The Settings (gear) menu gains a **"Card view options"** section listing
  the five fields — icon, last accessed, tab name, domain, window — each
  with a visibility checkbox (easy on/off) and up/down reorder arrows.
- The order also controls truncation priority: fields render in order and
  the overlay scrolls when they overflow, so higher-priority fields are the
  ones visible without scrolling.
- Configuration persists across sessions and applies to tab cards (window
  cards have their own fixed, minimal field set).

### Keyboard navigation (decided: full 2-D arrows)

Per Q6, card view gets true two-dimensional arrow navigation:

- **`←` `→` `↑` `↓`** move the selection through the grid; `↑`/`↓` jump by
  one visual row (computed from the current column count).
- **Sidebar↔tabs area switching moves to `Ctrl` `←` / `Ctrl` `→`** in both
  views, so the binding is consistent app-wide. In detail view, plain
  `↑`/`↓` keep moving through rows as today (plain `←`/`→` become no-ops
  there).
- `Enter` still activates the selected tab; the info banner and tour copy
  are updated to teach the new bindings.

### Persistence (settings schema)

`StorageData` in `types.ts` (and `services/storageService.ts`) gains:

```ts
tabViewMode?: 'detail' | 'card';        // default 'detail'
cardGrouping?: 'tab' | 'window';        // default 'tab'
cardWidth?: number;                     // px, default 240
cardMetadata?: { field: 'icon' | 'lastAccessed' | 'title' | 'domain' | 'window';
                 visible: boolean }[];  // default: all visible, order as above
```

## Requirement 3 — Manual window rename (decided: right-click menu)

Manual rename already exists (sidebar double-click and hover pencil icon,
persisting to storage with undo/redo). Per Q3, the intuitive control to add
is **right-click** — amended in the second Q&A round to open the window
**context menu** (Requirement 5) with **Rename** as its first item, rather
than jumping straight into the editor, so right-click behaves uniformly
across the app:

- **Rename (single window):** choosing Rename opens the same inline editor
  as today (Enter saves, Escape cancels, `handleRenameWindow` path,
  undo/redo history).
- **Rename (multiple windows checked):** when the right-clicked window is
  one of several checked windows, Rename asks for a **base name** and
  applies **sequential numbering** — `name1`, `name2`, … — to the checked
  windows in natural-sorted order. The batch is pushed as a **single**
  history entry, so one Undo reverts the whole batch.
- **Undo / Redo** entries appear in the window context menu (same
  `nameHistory` the sidebar buttons drive; disabled when unavailable).
- Available wherever a window is a first-class element: **sidebar window
  rows** and **window cards** in the new card view.
- The existing double-click and pencil-icon paths stay exactly as they are;
  the v001 discoverability extras (always-visible pencil, header rename)
  are dropped as unnecessary.

## Requirement 4 — Single click must not navigate

### Current behavior

In `components/TabListView.tsx` a row click runs
`onSelect(tab.id); onActivate(tab);` — every single click both selects the
row *and* switches Chrome to that tab, yanking focus away from the
dashboard.

### Design

- **Single click** — selects the row/card only (highlights it and shows it
  in the Preview Panel). No navigation.
- **Double click** — navigates (activates) the tab. Applies to both detail
  rows and tab cards. (On window cards, double-click drills into the
  window instead — see [Window cards](#window-cards).)
- Unchanged explicit navigation affordances: the **↗ Switch to Tab** hover
  button on each row/card, the **Enter** key on the keyboard-selected tab,
  and the ↗ button in the Preview Panel header.
- Copy that teaches the old behavior gets updated: the extension info
  banner and tour/user-guide text will say "double-click (or ↗ / Enter) to
  switch to a tab".

## Requirement 5 — Right-click context menus

Added in the second Q&A round (each candidate item was reviewed
individually). Three surfaces get a context menu; the preview panel was
considered and **excluded**.

### Tab menu (detail rows and tab cards)

| Item | Action |
|---|---|
| **Switch to Tab** | Navigate Chrome to the tab (same as double-click / ↗ / Enter). |
| **Move to Window ▸** | Submenu of all windows, natural-sorted, current window disabled; picking one moves the tab there. |
| **Move to New Window** | Moves the tab into a freshly created window. |
| **Copy URL** | Copies the tab's URL to the clipboard (first per-tab copy affordance in the app). |

Reviewed and **excluded**: Close Tab (the × hover button suffices), Copy
as Markdown link, and Wake Tab (superseded by Requirement 6).

**Multi-select semantics:** when the right-clicked tab is one of several
*checked* tabs, the menu's actions apply to **all checked tabs** and the
labels show the count ("Move 5 Tabs to Window ▸"). Right-clicking an
unchecked tab always acts on that tab alone.

### Window menu (sidebar rows and window cards)

| Item | Action |
|---|---|
| **Rename** | First item. Single window → inline editor; multiple checked windows → base name + sequential numbering (see Requirement 3). |
| **Undo / Redo** | The existing window-name history, also reachable here; disabled when unavailable. |
| **Focus Window in Chrome** | Brings the actual browser window to the front (`chrome.windows.update({focused: true})`) — previously there was no way to jump to a window itself, only to a tab in it. |
| **Auto-Name with AI** | AI-names just this window (existing Gemini path and history). |
| **Merge Checked Windows Here** | Shown when 2+ windows are checked: moves all their tabs into the right-clicked window — the merge modal's target-picking step becomes unnecessary. |
| **Move Checked Tabs Here** | Shown when 1+ tabs are checked: files them into the right-clicked window (the window-side complement of the tab menu's Move to Window ▸). |
| **Close Window** | Closes the window and all its tabs behind a "Close window and its N tabs?" confirmation (destructive; uses the existing `ConfirmModal`). |

Reviewed and **excluded**: View This Window's Tabs (left-click on the row
already does it).

### AI group menu (category headings in AI Organized view)

| Item | Action |
|---|---|
| **Check All Tabs in Group** | Ticks every tab in the category so toolbar bulk actions can target it. |
| **Move Group to New Window** | Materializes this one category as a real Chrome window, leaving all other windows untouched (lighter alternative to the all-or-nothing "Apply to Windows"). |

Reviewed and **excluded**: Sort Group by ▸ (column headers and the Sort
All dropdown already cover sorting).

### Implementation notes

- One shared `components/ContextMenu.tsx` renders all three menus:
  positioned at the cursor (clamped to the viewport), closes on
  click-outside / Escape / scroll, supports one submenu level and
  disabled/hidden items.
- `contextmenu` is intercepted (`preventDefault()`) **only** on tab rows,
  tab/window cards, sidebar window rows, and AI group headings — the
  browser's native right-click menu keeps working everywhere else
  (search box, preview panel, empty space).
- Menu items reuse the existing action handlers (`handleActivateTab`,
  `moveTabs`, `createWindowWithTabs`, `handleMerge`,
  `handleRenameWindow`, undo/redo) — no new tab-manipulation plumbing.

## Requirement 6 — Sleeping tabs wake automatically on settled selection

Replaces the proposed "Wake Tab" menu item, and answers "shouldn't waking
happen automatically when the user interacts with the tab?" — yes, with
one guard. Waking a discarded tab means **reloading the page** (network,
CPU, and the memory Chrome's Memory Saver had reclaimed), so selection
*traversal* must not wake tabs en masse: with ~170 tabs, holding `↓`
through a list of mostly-sleeping tabs would otherwise fire dozens of
simultaneous reloads.

**Rule:** when a sleeping tab becomes the selected tab — by click or by
keyboard — and **stays selected for ~400 ms**, it is woken automatically
(`wakeTab`) and its preview/thumbnail captured. Consequences:

- A deliberate single click feels fully automatic (the dwell is
  imperceptible).
- Arrow-keying through the list wakes nothing until the user pauses on a
  tab.
- Only the currently selected tab is ever auto-woken — never off-screen
  cards, never in bulk.
- The Preview Panel's "Wake up & preview" button remains as a manual
  fallback/retry; its "asleep" messaging changes to a transient "Waking
  tab…" state since waking now starts on its own.

## Resolved questions (from v001)

All seven v001 open questions were answered on 2026-07-31:

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Card = tab or window? | **Both**, user-selectable grouping toggle |
| 2 | Thumbnail approach | **Scaled HTML captures**, lazy + bounded |
| 3 | Rename control | **Right-click** opens inline rename |
| 4 | Sizing hotkeys | **`[` / `]`** (no browser-zoom conflict) |
| 5 | Spec filename format | **New format** `SPEC-<ver>-v<NNN>-<Name>`; old files renamed |
| 6 | Card-grid keyboard nav | **Full 2-D arrows**; area switch on `Ctrl` `←`/`→` |
| 7 | Sorting custom names | **Natural sort**, interleaved |

## Remaining notes & risks

1. **Thumbnail performance at ~170 tabs** remains the main implementation
   risk (mitigations specified above; fallback identified if they prove
   insufficient).
2. **Window-card double-click semantics** — this spec chose *drill into By
   Window view* for double-click and a ↗ button for focusing the real
   Chrome window. Flag during review of the build if you'd prefer
   double-click to focus the OS window instead.
3. **`[` / `]` are plain keys**: they are ignored while typing in any input
   (search box, rename editor), so there is no risk of hijacking text
   entry; outside inputs they are otherwise unused by the app.
4. **Tag/version mismatch (informational).** The latest commit (`c72a0a1`)
   is tagged `v4.0.3`, but `package.json`/`manifest.json` there still say
   `4.0.2` (no 4.0.3 bump commit was made). The first commit of this work
   should bump both files straight to `4.0.4`.
5. **Double-click reachability** — double-click-to-navigate is slower for
   rapid tab hopping and unfriendly to some accessibility setups, which is
   why the ↗ button and Enter remain first-class.

## Affected files (planned)

- `services/sortUtils.ts` — **new**: shared natural-sort comparator.
- `components/ContextMenu.tsx` — **new**: shared context-menu component
  (cursor positioning, submenu, disabled items, dismissal).
- `components/Sidebar.tsx` — numeric name sort; window context menu on
  window rows.
- `App.tsx` — numeric sort in `getSortedTabs`; view-mode / grouping /
  card-size / metadata state + persistence; `[`/`]` sizing hotkeys; 2-D
  arrow navigation + `Ctrl`-arrow area switching; toolbar toggles, slider,
  and card-view sort dropdown; context-menu state and action wiring
  (batch rename, merge-here, move-here, close window, group actions);
  settled-selection auto-wake timer; updated banner copy.
- `components/TabListView.tsx` — numeric sort; row click = select only,
  double-click = activate; tab context menu on rows.
- `components/TabCardView.tsx` — **new**: card grid (tab and window
  groupings), thumbnail iframes, metadata overlay, lazy capture queue,
  tab/window context menus on cards.
- `components/PreviewPanel.tsx` — auto-wake integration ("Waking tab…"
  state; manual wake button becomes fallback/retry).
- `components/CardViewOptions.tsx` (or inline in the settings menu) —
  **new**: field visibility/order editor.
- `services/tabService.ts` — thumbnail capture reuse (cache + concurrency
  around `getTabContent`).
- `services/storageService.ts`, `types.ts` — new persisted settings.
- `components/OnboardingTour.tsx` / tour copy in `App.tsx`,
  `components/UserGuideModal.tsx` — updated click/keyboard wording.
- `_quarto.yml` — this spec added to the book.
- `docs/spec-conventions.qmd` + three renamed 4.0.2 spec files — new
  filename convention (already applied alongside this revision).
- `package.json`, `manifest.json` — version bump to 4.0.4 (see note 4).

## Out of scope

- True pixel screenshots of background tabs (not possible with current
  Chrome extension APIs without focusing each tab).
- Auto-waking sleeping tabs to capture thumbnails.
- 2×2 mosaic thumbnails on window cards (possible later upgrade).
- Refactoring the three duplicated sort implementations into one (only the
  comparator is shared).
